introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Amos condemns those who cheat the poor and buy the needy for a pair of sandals. In the Gospel, Jesus tells the parable of the shrewd manager and warns that we cannot serve both God and money. Paul asks us to pray for everyone, including those in authority, for God wants all people to be saved. Let us be faithful in small things and serve God alone.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God raises the poor from the dust. Let us bring him our prayers for all people.
intentions: For the Church: that she may pray for all people, for God wills that all be saved. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who govern and hold authority: that they may work for justice and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the poor who are cheated and exploited: that God may defend them and that their rights may be respected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those in business and finance: that they may be honest and use their wealth for the common good. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be faithful in small things and use what we have for God and for others. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you call us to serve you alone and not money. Make us honest and generous, faithful in small things, and wise in using what you have entrusted to us. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: God and money
reflection.body:
Amos speaks against traders who can hardly wait for the holy days to end so that they can get back to business, "making the ephah small, and the shekel large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit." They "buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals." God says: "Surely I will never forget any of their works." Cheating the poor is not a small thing in God's eyes.

The Gospel parable is puzzling at first. A manager about to be dismissed reduces the debts of his master's debtors, so that they will welcome him later. And "His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely." Jesus is not praising dishonesty. He is pointing to the man's cleverness and energy in preparing for his future, and he says that "the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light." If people work so hard for earthly security, how much more should we use what we have for what lasts forever?

Then Jesus draws several lessons. Use money to make friends, especially among the poor, who will welcome you into eternal life. Be faithful in small things: "He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much." And above all, choose your master: "No servant can serve two masters... You aren't able to serve God and Mammon."

Paul asks that prayers be offered "for all men, for kings and all who are in high places." God "desires all people to be saved," and Christ "gave himself as a ransom for all." Our prayer should be as wide as God's love.

This week, look honestly at your use of money. Is it serving God and others, or has it become your master? Choose one way to be generous, and be faithful in some small, honest act.
